answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an copycat cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single inlet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a saffron, before it can post or attest. Forging 292 aliases therefore costs 497 bonds held for 21 days each, plus the ocean attestations those aliases can never earn. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
